prep.full_transcript: Hey traders, welcome back to the channel. Today I want to walk through two setups I actually trade during the New York session. The first one is my opening range breakout on the MNQ. I use the first fifteen minutes of the New York session on the five minute chart to build the opening range. Once that range is set, I wait for a full candle close above the range high before I go long. If instead price closes below the range low, I go short. I only take this setup between nine thirty and eleven in the morning Eastern time, and I skip the trade entirely on FOMC days because the volatility gets unpredictable. My stop sits just below the opening range low for longs, above the range high for shorts. I'm looking for at least two times my risk before I take profit, usually targeting the prior day's high or low. The second setup is completely different, it's a VWAP mean reversion fade on the ES. When price stretches more than two standard deviations away from the volume weighted average price, I start watching for a fade back toward VWAP. I want to see a bearish engulfing candle on the one minute chart before I short an overextended move above the upper band, and a bullish engulfing candle before I buy an overextended move below the lower band. I only take this trade when the overall daily range is already wide, because a narrow range day tends to just keep grinding instead of reverting. My stop goes just beyond the recent swing extreme, and my target is a full retrace back to VWAP itself. I avoid this setup completely during the first thirty minutes of the session because the volume weighted average price hasn't stabilized yet.
